body:
AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-backend#705 @ 5138947cd082328b81cbeb787833914431b22fc1 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES
A/B/C = 0/4/2

Agent 120, job AUD-OPUS-D6-120 (T4 audit lens). First Opus verdict on D2c (R-DISPUTE-PAUSE). Full review of the own diff `49d0b66e..5138947c` (1029+/380-, 1,409 of 1,500), composed with main ee55f814 and D1-D2b, against R-DISPUTE-PAUSE, owner rulings 5-7 (09:43 PDT 10-05) and the operator rulings accepted in JOBS120 B-DUNB.

**Checked and holding**
- Pause order: DB first under DunningState then ClientPurchase locks (access ends, marker, step 3, locked), then Stripe `pause_collection[behavior]=void` and open invoices marked uncollectible; client and coach notices go through the outbox and are retried while the pause holds (`cycleStillLive` accepts a locked marker cycle).
- Webhook writers: customer.subscription.updated and invoice.paid grant access only when `!disputePaused` under the purchase lock; `applyImmediateClear` now gets the webhook `tx` and re-reads the pause under the locks (B-S2, B-S3); v1 `recordResolution` leaves a marker cycle open (`dunning.service.ts:333`).
- A won closure on a recurring plan without access keeps `disputed` (`refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:1005-1017`).
- Restart: tenant check (`not_found` for any other coach), a canceled plan cannot restart.
- Ruling 6: an inquiry pauses like a dispute (`test/dunning-v2-dispute-pause.spec.ts:269`). Ruling 5: main's `flagFailedAfterApply` writes no access field. Ruling 7: not in this piece (C-680-16, later D2d).
- The webhook passes no dispute id until D4 (C-DUNMR-2), so the pause is inert at this head; the findings below are in the code D4 switches on.

## Findings

**B-705-1** `src/checkout/dunning-v2/dunning-v2.service.ts:1437-1440` with `:1320-1329` — when the restart's Stripe resume succeeded but the plan stays paused, the code re-pauses through `pauseBillingAtStripe`, which reuses the first pause's key `dunning_v2:dispute_pause:${purchaseId}:${cycleKey}`. Stripe returns the stored result for a key it has seen and only makes a new request once the key is at least 24 h old and pruned (https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests).
Counterexamples (probe, run below):
- (a) A second dispute lands while the coach's restart is in flight, on the day of the pause. The restart returns `new_dispute` and the DB stays paused with access ended. The re-pause is a replay, so Stripe billing stays resumed. The client is charged with no access.
- (b) The restart transaction throws after Stripe resumed (any DB error, for example P2034). The exception skips the re-pause, leaving Stripe resumed while the plan is paused.
- (c) The coach double-taps restart more than 24 h after the pause. Both requests pass the pre-checks. One restarts. The other gets `not_paused` and pauses again with the pruned key, which is now a real request. Billing is paused on a plan whose access was just restarted.
- Controls are green: the same race 2 days after the pause ends paused, and a plain restart resumes billing and grants access.

Fix rule: each restart attempt re-pauses with its own key, never the first pause's key. The re-pause runs on every exit where the plan stays paused, including a thrown transaction (try/finally). It is skipped when another restart resolved the cycle.

**B-705-2** `dunning-v2.service.ts:1348-1447` with `src/checkout/subscription-checkout.service.ts:507-525` — the restart resumes the paused subscription without checking whether the client already holds another live plan for the same package. Checkout counts a paused plan (status `disputed`, no access) as not live, so the client can start and pay a new subscription to the same package. A later coach restart then bills both.
Probe: p1 is paused and p2 is active and entitled for pkg-1. `restart(p1)` returns `restarted`, leaving two entitled, billing subscriptions for pkg-1.
Fix rule: the restart refuses with a coded reason when the client holds another live recurring plan (entitled, trialing or `LIVE_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES`) for the same package, and the coach is told why. The re-buy policy is operator decision 2.

**B-705-3** `dunning-v2.service.ts:1235-1238` with `src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:974-1001` — the coach restarts, and later the same dispute closes lost. Main's lost branch writes `chargeback_lost` and entitlement false. D2c's `onDisputeClosed` finds the obligation already applied (`dispute_already_applied`, reported `pause_kept`) and does not pause. Stripe keeps billing, and invoice.paid never grants access again (`purchaseHasEnded`). The client is charged every period with no access.
Probe: restart on Day 2, then main's handler gets `charge.dispute.closed` (lost), then the D2c closure runs. The purchase ends up `chargeback_lost` with no access while the Stripe fake is not paused.
Fix rule: on a lost closure of a recurring plan, access and billing must agree. The default (operator decision 1) is that the lost branch does not change access of a recurring plan the coach restarted after this dispute. The money reversal and the OR-111-1 payout notice still run. The alternative is that the closure re-applies the pause.

**B-705-4** `dunning-v2.service.ts:1128-1141` — `isDisputeCycleOpen`, and the `isDisputePaused` alias the webhook writers call, return false when FEATURE_DUNNING_V2 is off. The operator ruling (10:1x, accepted in JOBS120 B-DUNB) requires the dispute-pause check to run whether or not the flag is on, so a rollback cannot restore access to a paused plan. Main's `purchaseHasEnded` covers only a status in `REVOKED_STATUSES`. A closure-first pause (status `active`) or any later status rewrite loses that cover.
Probe: closure-first pause, then the flag goes off, then `customer.subscription.updated(active)`. The result is entitlement true.
Fix rule: the marker read ignores the flag; only the writes stay gated.

## Follow-ups (C)
- **C-705-5** `dunning-v2.service.ts:1330-1336` — invoices marked uncollectible at the pause stay uncollectible after a restart. The amount owed before the pause is never collected, and the coach is not told. Fix rule: the restart result and the coach copy say so, or reopening collection is an explicit coach choice.
- **C-705-6** `dunning-v2.service.ts:1381-1440` — nothing re-asserts the Stripe pause after a crash between a successful resume and the restart transaction (the builder's carried reconciler item). Fix rule: the sweep re-pauses a paused plan whose Stripe subscription has no `pause_collection`.
- Carried, not re-counted here: C-688-9 (lock order, on #688); C-687-9 (copy fallback, on #687); B-687-8 (dispute copy says "reversed" for an inquiry, on #687, which affects this piece's ruling-6 path); the builder's C-DUNMR-2 to C-DUNMR-5.

## Proof
- Lane https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37351686431 (branch `audit/AUD-OPUS-D6-120/705-probes-1`, deleted after the run) ran `test/aud-opus-d6-120-705.probe.spec.ts`; the source is kept at `ops/aud-120/AUD-OPUS-D6-120/`.
  - The new probe has 6 reds, each exactly at the asserted invariant: B-705-1 (a) line 137, (c) line 171 and (b) line 184; B-705-2 line 211; B-705-3 line 266; B-705-4 line 295. Its 3 controls are green.
  - In the same run, `dunning-v2-dispute-pause.spec.ts`, `dunning-v2-c680-18.spec.ts` and the builder-adapted D12-116 pause probe are green.
  - The R34D adaptation has 1 superseded red. Its C-680-19 case writes `paid` by hand, but the real handler now keeps `disputed`, which is green in `dunning-v2-c680-18.spec.ts:318-363`.
- The probe's Stripe fake models the documented idempotency semantics: a key seen within 24 h replays and applies nothing, and a pruned key makes a new request. The repo's own fake notes the same 24 h pruning (`test/support/fake-stripe-billing.ts:96`).
- PR checks at this head are all green (build-and-test, schema parity, RLS floor, rls-live, npm audit).

Evidence reused (G09): the builder-adapted pause versions of this lens's D12-116 and R34D-119 probes. In the D12-116 adaptation the builder stubbed the Stripe pause and rewrote four expectations to R-DISPUTE-PAUSE outcomes (`opened: true, reason: 'paused'`, `pause_kept` twice, cycle still open after closure); each rewrite matches the owner ruling, so the adaptation is accepted as a faithful replay. The R34D adaptation only adds cases. Builder lane 37344998517 was read for context only. The Sol D6-120 output was not read before this verdict.
